# UX Review & Persona Walkthrough Rules (ISO 9241 / CPUX)

When asked to review UX, improve usability, create/save personas, design a user flow, write usability test tasks, or build/refactor a UI component (`*.html`, `*.twig`, `*.vue`, `*.tsx`, `*.jsx`, `*.svelte`, `*View.java`):

1. **Persona Discovery, Persistence & Cognitive Walkthrough (Route A — Existing UI):**
   Check if `docs/ux/personas.md` exists in the repository and reuse those project personas. Otherwise, define 1 Primary Persona (task-focused, realistic context constraints like mobile use, glare, gloves, or time pressure) and 1 Edge-Case / Accessibility Persona (keyboard-only `Tab`/`Enter`/`Esc`, screen-reader, or 200% zoom) and trace their step-by-step path through the interface. When asked to create or save personas for project-wide reuse, persist them in `docs/ux/personas.md`.

2. **5-State Completeness Check:**
   Never ship Happy-Path-only UI. Verify and implement all 5 states:
   - `Empty State`: Motivating explanation why it is empty + direct primary Call-to-Action (CTA).
   - `Loading State`: `aria-busy="true"` on container, disabled submit trigger to prevent double-submits, layout-stable skeleton/spinner.
   - `Error / Offline State`: **Preserve all valid user input!** Never call `form.reset()` on validation error. Provide inline field recovery via `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby`, plus `role="alert"` summary.
   - `Partial / Overflow State`: Handle long German compound words (`break-words`/`hyphens: auto`), large lists, and missing optional data gracefully.
   - `Success State`: Clear feedback (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`) + inline **Undo** or explicit verb-based confirmation dialog (`"Mitglied löschen"` vs. `"Abbrechen"`, never `"OK/Cancel"`) for destructive actions.

3. **ISO 9241-110:2020 Interaction Principles:**
   - *Aufgabenangemessenheit (Suitability for the user's tasks):* Smart defaults/presets for the 80% case, `autocomplete`, `inputmode="numeric|tel"`.
   - *Selbstbeschreibungsfähigkeit (Self-descriptiveness):* Persistent `<label for="...">` (never placeholder-only inputs), visible format hints linked via `aria-describedby`.
   - *Erwartungskonformität (Conformity with user expectations):* Semantic `<button type="button|submit">` instead of `<div onClick>`, native `<dialog>`, logical `Tab` focus order.
   - *Erlernbarkeit (Learnability):* Progressive disclosure for advanced settings.
   - *Steuerbarkeit (Controllability):* Back-navigation without data loss, respect `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, use scalable `rem` units.
   - *Robuste Verwendung (Use error robustness):* Forgiving input parsers that strip spaces/formatting automatically (e.g., `.replace(/\s+/g, '')` on IBANs/phone numbers), plausibility limits, and destructive action guardrails.
   - *Benutzerbindung (User engagement):* Trustworthy micro-copy, zero dark patterns, motivating empty states.

4. **New Feature Conception — Problem vs. Solution Space (Route B — ISO 9241-210):**
   Structure new feature concepts into 4 strictly separated sections:
   - **1. Context of Use, Persona & As-Is Scenario (*Nutzungskontext, Persona & Ist-Szenario*)**
   - **2. User Needs (*Erfordernisse* — Problem Space):** Format as `"Als [Persona] benötige ich [Voraussetzung], um [Ziel zu erreichen]."` Never mention concrete UI widgets ("dropdown", "modal", "button") in this section!
   - **3. User Requirements (*Nutzungsanforderungen*):** Qualitative requirements + measurable ISO 9241-11 Quantitative targets (Effectiveness, Efficiency, Satisfaction).
   - **4. To-Be Walkthrough (*Soll-Szenario*) & Interaction Concept:** Concrete UI architecture, physical ergonomics, and all 5 UI states.

5. **Non-Leading Usability Test Tasks (Route C — CPUX Evaluation):**
   When writing tasks for usability test participants, embed them in a realistic scenario with concrete data and a verifiable end state, and **never quote literal UI labels** (menu items or button names) in the participant task text.

---
description: "Build editorial/magazine/report webpages on a GENUINE Müller-Brockmann modular grid (International Typographic Style) — not a decorative one. Encodes the discipline (columns + modules + baseline, grotesque type, flush-left, restrained black/white/red palette) AND the hard-won front-end engineering to make the grid real, visible, and verified: one CSS-variable source of truth, an interactive grid-toggle overlay that lives in the SAME content box as the content, subgrid \"bands\" so every element snaps to a column line, an 8px baseline lock, and runtime OPTICAL ALIGNMENT that puts display type's ink (not its box) on the line. Ships with a scaffold generator and a Puppeteer verification harness that proves 0px adherence."
alwaysApply: false
---

# Müller-Brockmann Grid Systems — built real, visible, and verified

Josef Müller-Brockmann (1914–1996), Zurich; *Grid Systems in Graphic Design* (1981) is the corpus. The grid is treated as an ethic, not decoration: **"The grid system is an aid, not a guarantee. It permits a number of possible uses and each designer can look for a solution appropriate to his personal style. But one must learn how to use the grid; it is an art that requires practice."** This skill encodes that discipline AND — the part most attempts get wrong — the front-end engineering to make the grid genuinely load-bearing on the web, plus a harness that PROVES it.

> **HARD GATE** — Do NOT ship a grid page without running `verify_grid.js` first. A visually plausible layout is not evidence of grid adherence — the harness is. Zero failing assertions is the only passing bar.

> Two real review notes this skill exists to prevent:
> 1. *"the grid is just slapped on top and misaligned"* → the overlay wasn't in the same content box as the content (see §2.2).
> 2. *"the H in the headline is off the grid"* → the headline's BOX was on the grid but its INK wasn't; large glyphs carry a side-bearing (see §2.6). **Box-on-grid ≠ ink-on-grid.**

---

## PART 1 — THE DISCIPLINE (decide before drawing)
- **Objective order.** The grid brings "constructive thought," legibility, and "objective and functional" design. Restraint is the point; the system, not the ego, organizes the page.
- **Modular grid.** Divide the type area into a field of **modules** — columns AND rows — separated by consistent **gutters**, inside defined **margins**. Text and images occupy whole modules. Müller-Brockmann specimens common field counts (8 / 20 / 32 fields). For the web, a **12-column grid + 8px baseline** is a robust general default; a **6×6 or 4×8 modular field grid** when you want visible rows too.
- **Baseline grid.** Vertical rhythm is sacred: **leading = a whole multiple of the baseline unit**, and every element snaps to it. This is what makes facing columns and images line up across the page.
- **Typography.** A **grotesque sans** (Akzidenz-Grotesk / Helvetica; on the web Inter, Helvetica Now, Archivo). **Flush-left, ragged-right.** Few sizes, large jumps in **scale** for hierarchy; objective, not expressive. Big **numerals/data set large** is a signature move.
- **Palette.** Pure white paper, near-black ink, **one accent — red is canonical**. Avoid the warm-cream "Claude look"; **never blue/purple gradients** (hard house rule).
- **White space + asymmetry.** Generous margins; asymmetric compositions held in tension by the grid.

---

## PART 2 — MAKE THE GRID REAL ON THE WEB (the load-bearing engineering)
`grid_tokens.py` emits this whole scaffold correctly; the rules below are why it's built the way it is.

### 2.1 One source of truth
Put every grid parameter in `:root` CSS variables — `--cols, --gutter, --margin, --bl (baseline), --lh (leading=3×bl), --maxw`. **Content and the overlay both read these same variables.** Never hand-author the overlay separately or it will drift.

### 2.2 The overlay MUST live in the SAME content box as the content  ← #1 bug
Failure mode: content sits in a centered `max-width` container while the overlay is a **full-width sibling** of the section. On any viewport wider than `--maxw`, the centered content and the full-width overlay no longer share column positions → "slapped on top / misaligned."
**Fix:** put `.guides` *inside* the same `.wrap`, and draw the column guides with `left/right = var(--margin)` and the **same** `repeat(var(--cols),1fr)` + `column-gap:var(--gutter)`. Then the overlay columns **are** the content columns at every width. Add left/right margin lines at `var(--margin)`.

### 2.3 Place every element by column LINE via subgrid bands
Don't eyeball spans. Each horizontal **band** spans all columns and re-exposes them:
```css
.band{grid-column:1 / -1; display:grid; grid-template-columns:subgrid; column-gap:var(--gutter); align-items:start;}
@supports not (grid-template-columns:subgrid){ .band{grid-template-columns:repeat(var(--cols),1fr);} }
```
Children place with `grid-column: <startline> / <endline>` (e.g. `1 / 6`, `6 / 13`). Every headline, paragraph, photo, caption now snaps to identical lines.

### 2.4 Lock vertical rhythm to the baseline
- Leading = `--lh` (e.g. 24px = 3×8). **Every line-height a multiple of the baseline, in px (not unitless) for display type** — unitless line-heights on large type push the box off the grid.
- Every margin/padding a multiple of the baseline. Spread top/bottom padding a multiple too, so content starts on a line.
- **Media heights = multiples of the leading** (e.g. 240/360/432/480px) so a photo's top AND bottom both land on lines.
- Hairline rules sit inside a baseline-height band, not free-floating.

### 2.5 The toggle (sizzle within the sizzle)
A control (button **+ `G` key**) toggles `body.grid-on`; overlay fades 0→1. Overlay draws: translucent **numbered column fields**, the **baseline** (major line every `--lh`, faint minor every `--bl`), and **margin lines**. Showing the real grid the page is built on IS the demo.

### 2.6 OPTICAL ALIGNMENT — display ink, not its box  ← the subtle bug
A 180px headline whose layout box is exactly on line 1 still looks misaligned against body text, because the letterform's **ink** is inset by its **left side-bearing**. Cure at runtime:
```js
// after document.fonts.ready and on resize:
var cvs=document.createElement('canvas'),ctx=cvs.getContext('2d');
document.querySelectorAll('.masthead,.numeral,.shead h2,.h2b').forEach(function(el){
  el.style.marginLeft='0px';
  var cs=getComputedStyle(el),ch=(el.textContent||'').trim()[0]; if(!ch) return;
  if(cs.textTransform==='uppercase') ch=ch.toUpperCase();
  ctx.font=cs.fontStyle+' '+cs.fontWeight+' '+cs.fontSize+' '+cs.fontFamily; ctx.textAlign='left';
  var abl=ctx.measureText(ch).actualBoundingBoxLeft;     // +ve = ink overhangs left of box
  if(isFinite(abl)) el.style.marginLeft=abl.toFixed(2)+'px'; // shift box so INK lands on the line
});
```
Apply to the masthead, big numerals, and section headlines. It scales with fluid type (re-runs on resize) and uses the **actually-loaded** font, so it's correct in the user's browser.
**CRITICAL measurement caveat:** side-bearing is **font-specific**. If you measure with the wrong font you get the wrong nudge. Headless/sandbox Chrome usually lacks the webfont, so canvas falls back to a different grotesque (measured **−16px on the fallback vs −7px on real Inter** for the same `H`). To verify optics offline you must **embed the real webfont** via `@font-face` (local TTF). In production the runtime JS measures the loaded font and is correct.

---

## PART 3 — VERIFY (don't trust, measure)  → `verify_grid.js`
Render with headless Chrome (Puppeteer) and assert, at **several widths including > and < `--maxw`** (to catch centered-container drift, e.g. 1440 / 1180 / 900):
1. **Column adherence** — every placed `.band > *` left snaps to a column START and right to a column END (~0px). **Exclude the optically-aligned display elements** from this box check (their box is intentionally side-bearing-offset; they're validated in step 4). **Gotcha:** build

# agent-context-doctor — Cursor Rules

You are an **implementation agent** for this project. Focus on implementation only — product strategy is out of scope.

## Hard rules

- No LLM calls, no telemetry, no external network requests
- No authentication or credential handling
- No web server or browser UI
- Do not rename `acd`, `audit`, or `list` commands
- Do not break the `AuditResult` JSON shape or `.acdrc` schema backward compatibility

## Before finishing any task

Run and confirm these all pass:

```bash
pnpm format:check
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

## Code style

- TypeScript strict mode — no `any`, no `ts-ignore`
- Pure functions for all audit checks in `src/audit/checks/`
- Tests in `tests/*.spec.ts` using vitest
- No comments that narrate what the code does

## Final report format

Always return:

- Files changed (list)
- Commands run and their output
- Tests added
- Known limitations

description: "Mandatory Multi-Archetype Live Benchmark Protocol: Prevents AI from guessing or patching from static memory. Forces live web synthesis across world-class design, editorial, storytelling, and engineering references (Apple HIG, Stripe, Linear, Pentagram, Kinfolk, Vox, Cloudflare, AWS Well-Architected) before fixing or building."
globs: "*"
alwaysApply: true

# 01 - Multi-Archetype World-Class Benchmark Protocol (`RULE-BENCHMARK-FIRST`)

## PART A: ENGLISH SPECIFICATION

### 1. Core Invariant: Zero Memory-Only Patching

Whenever the user critiques an output, points out a flaw (in UI/UX, Typography, Motion Graphics, Copywriting, Product Strategy, or System Architecture), or proposes a new feature or design direction:

1. **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN - Memory-Only Guessing**: Never rely solely on frozen pre-training weights to invent a makeshift patch. Autoregressive sampling from static memory defaults to the statistical average of mediocre public repositories (purple neon gradients, nested bordered cards, fake sci-fi labels like `//`, `·`, `#REF`, `[01]`, or robotic filler prose).
2. **Step 1 - Mandatory Multi-Archetype Live Benchmark**: Immediately invoke live web search, URL inspection, or browser tools (`search_web`, `read_url_content`, or equivalent) to survey multiple world-class reference archetypes across four distinct domains:
   - **Domain 1 - Product & Interface Design**: *Apple Human Interface Guidelines (HIG), Stripe Press, Linear, Raycast, Vercel*
   - **Domain 2 - Editorial & Brand Identity**: *Pentagram, Kinfolk, The New York Times Visual Investigations, Monocle*
   - **Domain 3 - Visual Storytelling & Motion**: *Ordinary Folk, Vox, Johnny Harris, Kurzgesagt, Lemmino, Cleo Abram*
   - **Domain 4 - Engineering & System Architecture**: *Stripe API Design, Cloudflare Architecture, AWS Well-Architected Framework, Designing Data-Intensive Applications*
   - Never lock into a single narrow template. Survey at least **2 to 3 distinct archetypes** and extract task-specific mechanisms: spatial ratios and typographic scales for UI/motion tasks, narrative flow and concrete anchors for copywriting/strategy, and idempotency contracts, failure modes, latency budgets, and operability for engineering/architecture tasks.
3. **Step 2 - Objective Self-Critique vs. Global Standard**: Present a concise, transparent diagnostic comparison to the user before or alongside the implementation:
   - *Why did the previous attempt fail or feel cheap?* (Identify the exact root defect: e.g., fell into Sci-Fi Greebling, used nested bordered cards, relied on passive nominalized prose, or lacked explicit failure/latency boundaries).
   - *How do top-tier studios or principal engineering teams solve the root problem structurally?*
4. **Step 3 - World-Class Execution & Verifiable Audit Trail**: Implement the distilled mechanism directly into the codebase or document using measurable constraints (exact pixel spacing, contrast ratios, non-linear type scale, or deterministic API contracts). Before delivery, record each selected reference's title, URL, access date, distilled mechanism, and the exact file/line change that applies it.

---

### 2. Operational Domain Triage & Benchmark Selection Matrix

Use the decision matrix below to select the mandatory reference archetypes for any incoming user task:

| Task Category | Primary Archetype Domain | Secondary Cross-Pollination Domain | Concrete Structural Mechanism to Extract | Mandatory Quantitative Parameter |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. SaaS Dashboard & Metric Cards** | *Linear, Stripe, Apple HIG* | *Pentagram* (Editorial grid clarity) | Single-container card hierarchy, background luminance separation, zero nested boxes. | `>= 70% Open Canvas`, `16px-28px` padding, `12.6:1` AAA night contrast (`#E6E4DD` on `#090A0F`). |
| **2. Landing Page & Hero Section** | *Vercel, Raycast, Stripe Press* | *Kinfolk* (Negative space cadence) | High-contrast headline focal anchor, restrained 1-accent callout pill, generous CTA breathing room. | Headline `32px-48px`, lead copy `16px-18px` (`<= 65ch`), `28px` vertical CTA separation. |
| **3. Long-Form Technical Essay & Docs** | *NYT Visual Investigations, Stripe Docs* | *Vox* (Progressive visual disclosure) | Topic-Comment active sentences, symmetrical numerical comparisons, collapsible deep-dive blocks. | `15-28 words` average sentence, `45-word` hard cap, zero em-dashes (`U+2014`). |
| **4. 1080p Video Essay & Slide Canvas** | *Ordinary Folk, Vox, Johnny Harris* | *Apple HIG* (Title-safe legibility) | Paused act dividers, tactile visual anchors, strict subtitle safe-zone clearance. | `1920x1080` frame: X margin `>= 64px-88px`, Top `>= 42px-54px`, Bottom content `y <= 875px`. |
| **5. REST / RPC API & Webhook Backend** | *Stripe API Design, Cloudflare* | *AWS Well-Architected* | Idempotency keys, structured machine-readable error envelopes, explicit timeout budgets. | P99 latency budget defined, exponential backoff with jitter, deterministic status codes. |
| **6. Database Schema & State Mutations** | *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* | *Stripe Engineering* | Transactional atomicity, append-only audit logs, explicit migration rollback paths. | Zero silent catch blocks, strict schema validation at ingress boundary. |
| **7. Form Checkout & Onboarding Flow** | *Stripe Checkout, Linear Onboarding* | *Apple HIG* | Progressive disclosure, inline validation after blur, minimum input field friction. | `<= 3-4` visible fields per step, `>= 44px` touch target height on mobile viewports. |
| **8. Design System Token Architecture** | *Apple HIG, Linear, Kinfolk* | *Vercel Geist* | Semantic surface/text/accent tokens locked to W3C relative luminance formulas. | Max 1 primary surface, 1 text hierarchy (`95%` / `65%`), 1 accent hue (`#F7B957`). |

---

### 3. 10-Pair Side-by-Side Comparison: ❌ Forbidden vs. ✅ Required

| # | Operational Scenario | ❌ Forbidden (Memory-Only Anti-Pattern) | ✅ Required (World-Class Benchmark Standard) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **User says: "This card looks boring, make it look more technical."** | Guessing from memory and adding `// SYS.REF:01`, neon cyan borders, status dots `•`, and `10px` monospace tags. | Benchmarking *Linear* & *Apple HIG*: using a single `#090A0F` card (`12px` radius, `3px` `#F7B957` bottom accent, `28px` padding, `34px` metric). |
| **2** | **User critiques: "The dark mode text feels hard to read."** | Switching text to pure `#FFFFFF` on pure `#000000` (`21:1` contrast) from memory, triggering astigmatic halation. | Benchmarking ophthalmic dark-mode ergonomics & WCAG 2.1 AAA: locking `#E6E4DD` warm off-white on `#090A0F` deep obsidian (`12.6:1`). |
| **3** | **User asks for a pricing comparison section.** | Generating a generic 3-column Bootstrap table with 15 checkmark rows, rainbow badges, and flashing timers. | Benchmarking *Stripe* & *Raycast*: 2 crisp tiers, clear value metric differentiation, 1 highlighted recommended tier, `>= 70%` open canvas. |
| **4** | **User complains: "My article introduction sounds like ChatGPT."** | Re-writing from memory using synonyms (`delve` -> `explore deeply`, keeping passive nominalizations and em-dashes). | Benchmarking *The New York Times* & *GS. Cao Xuân Hạo*: stripping nominalizations, opening with a sensory scene or `70% vs. 13%` data anchor. |
| **5** | **User reports an intermittent webhook duplicate payment bug.** | Adding a naive `setTimeout` delay or local boolean flag in memory without researching distributed idempotency. | Benchmarking *Stripe API Idempotency*: implementing an `Idempotency-Key` header with atomic database upsert and 24-hour key retention. |
| **6** | **User asks to animate a scene transition or UI modal.** | Applying linear `duration-500` CSS transitions or bouncy cartoon keyframes (`scale(1.3)`) from static memory. | Benchmarking *Ordinary Folk* & *Apple HIG*: using damped spring physics (`stiffness: 220, damping: 26`) with subtle `8px

# Cursor AI Rules

> These rules are loaded automatically for this project. See `AGENTS.md` for full details.

## Core Directives

1. **Read AGENTS.md before any task** — All rules are defined there
2. **Read DEEPDIVE.md** — System architecture narrative
3. **Follow every section** — Core principles, commit protocol, testing, linting, etc.

## Critical Enforcements

### Pre-Commit Checklist
```bash
ruff check .
ruff format .
vulture .
mypy .
```
**Do not commit until all pass.** (Section 9)

### Required Folders
Every project MUST have:
- `tests/` — All tests + random scripts (in `.gitignore`)
- `docs/` — Architecture documentation
- `research/` — Whitepapers, references

### Commit Style
Human-sounding, WHY-focused messages. Example:
```
api: Added JWT refresh to prevent 401 loops

The token refresh had a race condition where concurrent requests
could trigger multiple refresh calls. Added mutex lock around auth state.
```
See Section 15 for the full pattern.

### PR Standards (Section 33)
- 800 lines max, 500 for complex logic
- Single feature per PR
- Use the PR template (Section 35)

### AI Code Quality (Section 34)
Self-check: think first, spot laziness, uncertainty, bloat.

### Pre-Commit Hooks (Section 37)
Mandatory. Install once: `pre-commit install`. Hooks run on every commit.

### Decision Ladder (Section 50.1)
Before any implementation: YAGNI → stdlib → native → existing dep → one line → minimum.

### Tradeoff Comments (Section 50.2)
For every intentional shortcut, document with `# ponytail: <what> / # Upgrade to <what> if <trigger>`.

## Prohibited
- No PRs/issues/GitHub activity without explicit user approval (Section 2)
- No dead code, unused imports, silent exception handlers (Section 1)
- No commits without running lint/vulture sweep first (Section 9)
- No mutable default arguments, bare excepts, eval/exec (Section 27.2)
- No force push to shared branches (Section 36.2)
- No PRs over 800 lines (Section 33)
- No skipping pre-commit hooks (Section 37)

## Validation
Before marking complete:
- [ ] Tests pass
- [ ] No vulture findings
- [ ] Type check clean
- [ ] DEEPDIVE.md updated if needed
- [ ] Human commit message
- [ ] PR under 800 lines
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks passed
- [ ] AI anti-pattern self-check passed
- [ ] Decision ladder applied
- [ ] Tradeoff comments for shortcuts

# Cursor AI Rules for Betting Brain Platform
# https://github.com/nolarose1968/ffffff/blob/main/.cursorrules

## One File to Rule Them All

This `.cursorrules` file is the **single source of truth** for all AI-generated code.

**Benefits:**
- ✅ No confusion - everyone follows the same patterns
- ✅ Version control - every change is tracked
- ✅ Automatic application - Cursor applies rules to matching files
- ✅ Machine readable - front-matter enables tooling integration

**Alternative:** Cursor ≥ 0.45 also supports `.cursor/rules/` folder for larger projects.

## Core Development Rules

### Bun Runtime (CRITICAL)
- Use `bun` commands exclusively (not npm/yarn/node)
- Use Bun Test (not Vitest/Jest)
- Use Bun file APIs (not Node.js fs)
- Use processManager for all process spawning
- Leverage Bun native APIs (crypto, compression, etc.)

### File Organization
- Root directory: Only 9 essential files allowed
- Documentation: All docs in `docs/` (except README.md, LICENSE, CLAUDE.md)
- Scripts: All in `scripts/`
- Tools: All in `tools/`
- Status files: All in `docs/`

### File Naming
- Use lowercase kebab-case for all files/directories
- Test files: `*.test.ts` (preferred)
- Special cases: MCP handlers use camelCase to match tool names
- Never create backup files (*.backup, *.old, *.bak)

## API & Endpoint Patterns

### Request Handling
- Always generate requestId: `Date.now().toString(36)`
- Always include CORS headers for dashboard access
- Always handle OPTIONS preflight requests
- Always log with requestId prefix: `[${requestId}] ...`

### Error Handling
- Use standardized error classes from `src/utils/error-handler.ts`
- Always use try-catch or asyncHandler wrapper
- Always return structured error responses
- Never expose internal details in error messages

### Database Queries
- Always use parameterized queries (`.bind()`)
- Never use string interpolation in SQL
- Always cast D1 results with `as unknown as`
- Always handle database errors

## Security Patterns

### Input Validation
- Always validate all inputs before processing
- Use Zod schemas for request validation
- Never trust user input
- Always sanitize output to prevent XSS

### Production Security
- Never use `parseFloat()` on stakes (use `Number()`)
- Always use parameterized D1 queries
- Respect queue batch limits (100 messages max)
- Always free WASM memory in finally blocks
- Use explicit UTC timestamps (not `new Date()`)

## Testing Patterns

### Bun Test Usage
- Import from `bun:test` (not vitest/jest)
- Always cleanup processes in `afterEach`/`afterAll`
- Use `{ results: [...] }` for D1 database mocks
- Reset mock implementations in `beforeEach`
- Use explicit try-catch for async error testing

### Test Organization
- Unit tests: `tests/unit/*.test.ts`
- Integration tests: `tests/integration/*.test.ts`
- Use descriptive test names
- Group related tests in `describe` blocks

## Cloudflare Workers

### Environment Bindings
- ANALYTICS: Main betting analytics database
- KV namespaces: BET_TICKER_RAW, TOKEN_STORE, USER_STORE
- Queues: LINE_INGRESS, STEAM_WEBHOOK, STEAM_QUEUE
- Analytics Engine: ANALYTICS_ENGINE

### Performance
- CPU limit: 50ms per request
- Use `ctx.waitUntil()` for non-blocking operations
- Implement cost guards for resource limits
- Use rate limiting (10 req/s per IP)

## MCP Integration

### MCP Server Patterns
- Use JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over stdio
- Register tools with `registerTool(name, description, inputSchema, handler)`
- Return MCP response format: `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: '...' }] }`
- Use standard JSON-RPC error codes (-32700 parse, -32600 invalid, -32601 method not found, -32602 invalid params, -32603 internal)
- Never use external MCP SDK if Bun + Zod suffices

### Tool Development
- Create handler in `src/mcp/handlers/`
- Register in `toolRegistry.ts`
- Define in `tools.ts` with schema
- Always validate args before database queries
- Return `MCPToolResult` format

### Sports API Validation
- Validate all sports data with Zod schemas
- Required fields: eventId, timestamp, metric, value
- Use metadata for market, source, volume
- Write to ANALYTICS_ENGINE with proper blobs/doubles/indexes
- Handle CORS for cross-origin requests

### Testing MCP Tools
- Use direct handler testing first
- Test with `bun scripts/test-handlers-direct.ts`
- HTTP testing via `/mcp` endpoint

## Sports API Integration

### Data Fetching
- Use MCP `live-odds` tool for odds (never hard-code API calls)
- Aggregate ≥ 2 bookmakers for accuracy (Pinnacle + Bet365)
- Cache live data ≤ 30s in SPORTS_CACHE KV
- Sports enum: nba, nfl, mlb, nhl only
- Markets enum: moneyline, spread, total only

### Data Ingestion
- Push via `push-sports-data` MCP tool after every fetch
- Ingest endpoint requires JWT signed with JWT_SECRET
- Rate limit: 100 req/min per IP on `/ingest`
- Validate eventId, timestamp, odds (required fields)
- Include source and volume in metadata

### API Key Rotation
- Use rotateSecret() for daily key rotation
- Pattern: PINNACLE_KEY_1, PINNACLE_KEY_2, PINNACLE_KEY_3
- Rotation based on day of year % 3 + 1
- Never commit actual keys to repo

## Browser Extension

### Manifest v3
- Use service worker lifecycle
- Handle message passing correctly
- Implement proper storage management
- Follow security best practices
- Never use eval() or innerHTML

## CI/CD Patterns

### Local Development
- Use `bun run ci` for full pipeline
- Use `bun run ci:quick` for fast checks
- Always use timeouts (job and command level)
- Cache dependencies for speed
- Report results clearly

### Process Management
- Always use `processManager.spawn()`
- Always set timeouts for processes
- Always cleanup in finally blocks
- Never leave zombie processes

## Code Quality

### Documentation
- Reference rules with stable GitHub links
- Use `mdc:` links for project files
- Keep documentation in `docs/`
- Update INDEX.md when adding docs

### ast-grep Integration
- Use `sg scan` for security checks
- Enforce SQL injection prevention
- Check for unstructured logs
- Validate CORS headers
- Monitor hardcoded URLs

## Automation Layer (v3.2.0+)

### Forest CLI & Monitoring
- Always run `bun run forest` before pushing to verify grove health
- Check specific status: `bun run forest h|f|r|a` (health/fresh/release/analytics)
- Use Forest CLI in CI for automated status reporting

### Analytics Testing
- Use `createAnalyticsEngineStub()` for analytics tests—**never mock ANALYTICS_ENGINE directly**
- Import from `tests/utils/analytics-engine-stub.ts`
- Violation detection: `bun run guard:analytics` (fails CI if violated)

### Dashboard Management
- Dashboard changes must pass `bun run dashboard:all` locally before commit
- Dashboards auto-deploy on release tag push
- Grafana auto-imports on release (if configured)
- README auto-updates with version and links

### Release Management
- Use Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, chore:, docs:)
- Release automation: `bun run release [patch|minor|major]`
- Dry run first: `bun run release:dry`
- Tag push triggers full automation (bump, deploy, notify)

### Dependency Management
- Dependency updates happen automatically every Monday
- **Do not bump dependencies manually** (use freshness workflow)
- Review weekly PR from automation
- Emergency updates: `bun run freshness` then create PR

### Health Monitoring
- Worker health checked every 6 hours automatically
- Manual check: `bun run health:ping`
- Slack alerts sent on failure (if configured)
- Endpoints: `/health` and `/metrics` auto-deployed

- [Complete Rules Guide](https://github.com/nolarose1968/ffffff/blob/main/docs/CURSOR_RULES.md)
- [API Reference](https://github.com/nolarose1968/ffffff/blob/main/docs/REST_API_REFERENCE.md)
- [Testing Guide](https://github.com/nolarose1968/ffffff/blob/main/docs/TESTING_STATUS.md)

---
description: Supabase RLS, grants and keys. Apply when writing Supabase migrations, policies, grants, views, functions, or client code that reads or writes Supabase data.
globs: supabase/**/*.sql, **/migrations/**/*.sql, **/*.sql
alwaysApply: false
---

# Supabase RLS and grants: rules for writing secure migrations

Apply these whenever you create or change a Supabase table, view, function, policy or grant, or write client code that reads or writes Supabase data.

## Every table in an exposed schema
- Enable RLS in the **same migration** that creates the table: `alter table public.x enable row level security;`. A table must never exist without it.
- RLS on with no policy denies everything. Add the policies the app needs in that same migration.
- Grant explicitly, per table, only to the role that needs it and only the operations the app uses:
  `grant select on public.x to authenticated;`
  New tables don't get automatic grants for `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` (Supabase change of Oct 30, 2026); without a grant the API returns `42501 permission denied for table`.
- Never "fix" a 42501 with `grant ... on all tables in schema public to anon, authenticated`. It also grants every table with RLS off, making it readable and writable with the public anon key.
- Grant to `anon` only for data that signed-out visitors should read, and pair it with a policy that allows exactly that.

## Policies
- Write one policy per operation (`for select`, `for insert`, `for update`, `for delete`) and name the role with `to authenticated` (or `to anon`).
- Wrap `auth.uid()` as `(select auth.uid())` so Postgres evaluates it once per query, not per row.
- INSERT policies need `with check` (they can't have `using`, and without `with check` they let no rows in). On UPDATE, write both `using` (which rows) and `with check` (what they may become). If `with check` is missing, Postgres checks the new row against `using`, which is only safe when `using` is as strict as what a row may become: with an `or` (shared or team rows) a row can be handed to another user.
- No policy protects a column it doesn't mention: an owner policy on `user_id` won't stop a user from changing `is_admin` on their own row. For sensitive columns, grant `update` only on the columns users may change (`grant update (body) on public.notes to authenticated;`).
- UPDATE also needs a SELECT policy for the same rows, or it silently affects 0 rows.
- Never use `using (true)` / `with check (true)` on private data. Allow it only for data that is public on purpose, and say so in a comment.
- A policy must not query the table it protects (that raises `42P17 infinite recursion detected in policy`). Put the lookup in a `security definer` function in a **non-exposed** schema (e.g. `private`), with `set search_path = ''`, schema-qualified names, a filter on `(select auth.uid())`, `revoke all ... from public` and `grant execute` only to `authenticated`.
- Multi-tenant data: scope rows to the caller's tenant through a membership lookup (the helper above), never through a value the client sends.

## Views, functions, other schemas
- Views run with the owner's privileges by default and skip RLS. Create them with `with (security_invoker = true)`, or don't expose them.
- `security definer` functions bypass RLS: keep them out of exposed schemas unless they are meant as an API, and validate the caller inside.
- A table in a non-`public` schema needs that schema in the Data API's exposed schemas, `grant usage on schema ... to <role>`, plus the table grant and RLS.

## Keys and clients
- The `anon` / publishable key is public by design; RLS is what protects data.
- Never put the `service_role` / `sb_secret_...` key in frontend code, `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` / `VITE_*` env vars, or anything shipped to the browser. It bypasses all RLS. Use it only on the server.
- On the server, create the Supabase client from the user's session (request cookies) so `auth.uid()` resolves; otherwise queries run as `anon`.

## Errors and what they mean
- `42501 permission denied for table|schema`: missing grant or schema usage (before RLS runs).
- `new row violates row-level security policy`: an INSERT/UPDATE failed `with check`.
- `PGRST116 Cannot coerce the result to a single JSON object` with `.single()` and a row that exists: RLS is hiding it from this caller (or there's no session). Use `.maybeSingle()` only when 0 rows is a normal answer.
- An update or delete that returns no error but changes nothing: no matching UPDATE/DELETE (or SELECT) policy. Chain `.select()` to see the affected rows.
- `PGRST205 Could not find the table ... in the schema cache`: wrong name/schema, schema not exposed, or a stale cache (`notify pgrst, 'reload schema';`).

## Prove it
- Test policies as the real roles (`anon`, `authenticated` as user A and as user B), not in the SQL editor, which bypasses RLS.
- Check what the API roles can reach:
  ```sql
  select c.relname,
         has_table_privilege('anon', c.oid, 'select') as anon_can_read,
         c.relrowsecurity as rls_on
  from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
  where n.nspname = 'public' and c.relkind = 'r'
  order by 1;
  ```
  `anon_can_read = true` with `rls_on = false` means the table is public.
- Gate it in CI: `npx airlock-rls` fails the build when a table ships without RLS or with an always-true policy.

Guides with tested SQL for each rule: https://shipsealed.com/rls/

# Writing instructions for models

These habits apply whenever you write or edit text that another model will follow: prompts, system prompts, skills, rules, `CLAUDE.md`, and `AGENTS.md`.

- Describe the behavior you want. Name the target with a number, a scope, or a concrete alternative: "Answer in under 100 words." "Cite sources from A, B, and C." "Verify changes with `npm run typecheck`."
- When asked to take something out of instruction text, delete every sentence about it, then rebuild the section from a short brief of what the text covers now. The finished section reads as if it was written that way from the start.
- State each rule once, as one calm, plain sentence. That is the form a model gives the most weight.
- Keep genuine limits on irreversible actions, security, privacy, and legal boundaries. State each one once, next to the instruction it guards, with the reason and a fallback: "Ask before force-pushing, because it rewrites shared history."
- For a full audit of a file, with parallel subagent reviewers and a leak check on the rewrite, run `/pink-elephant <file>`.

# Identity

You are a senior staff engineer and tech lead on **REPLACE:PROJECT_NAME**. You own correctness, quality, and maintainability. Think before acting, verify before claiming success, and push back plainly on flawed assumptions — a trusted advisor, not a yes-machine.

---

# AI Agent Rules — REPLACE:PROJECT_NAME

> **Bootstrap:** copy `templates/cursorrules.template` → repo-root `.cursorrules`, then replace every `REPLACE:` token.

## Core Principles (ALWAYS APPLY — override all else, non-negotiable)

1. **Correct the user.** Be truthful; never agree to be agreeable. If an approach is flawed, say so and offer a better path.
2. **Never claim PASS on failing output.** Report any test/build/validation error explicitly with the relevant output.
3. **Verify before "done".** Run tests/build/lint appropriate to the change; all provided tests must pass. If you can't verify, state what you checked and what's unverified.
4. **Optimal path.** Most efficient, reliable, maintainable option; no over-engineering; no edits to unrelated files.
5. **Evidence-first, never memory-first.** Back every non-trivial claim with file evidence (path + snippet), runtime output, or live docs. Missing evidence → mark **Unverified** and gather it. Banned without evidence: "this is fixed", "already implemented", "tests pass", "works now".
6. **Assumption ledger** (substantial tasks): state Confirmed facts / Inferences / Unknowns; never collapse inference into fact.
7. **Completion gate** (cannot skip): claim done only when changes are applied, checks ran, output shows no blocking failure, and residual risks are listed. If checks can't run, say why + give manual steps.
8. **Per-message permission only.** Explicit human approval never becomes standing or permanent. Each `git commit`/`push`, file delete, DB drop/truncate/wipe, protected-file edit, or history rewrite needs approval in the **same message** that requests it — earlier chat approval does not carry forward.
9. **Brevity cap + escalation gate** (cannot skip). The two halves are one rule: stay under budget, and ask before exceeding it.

   **Budget:** chat prose ≤ **150 words** per response, excluding code blocks, diffs, command output, and the three mandatory handoff sections. Content inside generated artifacts, plans, SPECs, and reports follows its own template and does not consume the chat budget.

   **Escalation gate:** if the complete answer needs more than the budget, or the task would expand beyond a literal reading of the request (extra audits, subagents, multi-track investigation, refactors, hardening beyond the ask), **stop and ask first**. Deliver the short answer plus one line naming what the long version would cover. Never deliver the long version unrequested, and never ask for expansion after the work is already done and dumped.

   This rule governs **volume**, not just style. Banned: unrequested option matrices, multi-table comparisons, restating the request, narrating reasoning, and re-explaining evidence already given. Kept: the evidence citation needed to support a claim (Principle 5), a failing output (Principle 2), and the handoff sections.

---

## Change safety (mechanical)

Default to **minimal diffs**. Run before commit / `@code-implementation complete`:

| Gate | Command | Fail when |
|------|---------|-----------|
| Touch scope | `bash scripts/touch-scope-verify.sh` | File outside `.work/touch-scope` or iteration **Files** |
| Blast radius | `bash scripts/blast-radius-check.sh` | `risk: high` (cross-area or oversized diff) |
| Protected surfaces | `standards/PROTECTED_SURFACES.json` + `.work/PROTECTED_SURFACES.json` + §Protected Files | High-blast path without owner approval |
| Tests | `bash scripts/framework-verify.sh` (see `DOCS_TECH_STACK.md`) | Non-zero exit |

**Declare scope first:** copy `templates/work/touch-scope.template` → `.work/touch-scope`, or `@code-implementation plan` with **Files** per task. **MOD-06** required for agent-authored code (`concepts/README.md` § Trigger table); `human-only` opt-out only when the human declares it in the same message. **No collateral edits** — no drive-by refactors, dependency bumps, or "while I'm here" changes.

---

## Required Context Files

**Lost? Read [`START_HERE.md`](START_HERE.md) first.**

**Free-text entry:** don't know which skill to run? Invoke `@ai-director - <what you want>` (Agent OS), `@ui-director` (`.ai.ui`), `@biz-director` (`.ai.biz`), `@soc-director` (`.ai.soc`), or `@x-director` for cross-framework work.

### Frameworks registry (cross-framework discovery)

Sister frameworks are siblings on disk; `.ai/` is self (self-hosted). Paths resolve at runtime. Sister dirs auto-discover as `<source basename with <fw> inserted before its last .segment>` (e.g. `pilo.ai.ui.logicbison` for this `pilo.ai.logicbison` source) or legacy `.ai.<fw>` — see path resolution below.

| Framework | Director | Path | Bootstrap artifact |
|-----------|----------|------|--------------------|
| `.ai` (Agent OS) | `@ai-director` | *this directory* | `skills/README.md` |
| `.ai.ui` (UI Design OS) | `@ui-director` | `../.ai.ui` | `../.ai.ui/skills/README.md` |
| `.ai.biz` (Business OS) | `@biz-director` | `../.ai.biz` | `../.ai.biz/skills/README.md` |
| `.ai.soc` (Social OS) | `@soc-director` | `../.ai.soc` | `../.ai.soc/skills/README.md` |
| `.ai.cto` (CTO Professor OS) | `@cto-director` | `../.ai.cto` | `../.ai.cto/skills/README.md` |
| `.ai.flutter` (Flutter Agent OS) | `@flutter-director` | `../.ai.flutter` | `../.ai.flutter/skills/README.md` |
| `.ai.mlt` (MLT Agent OS) | `@mlt-director` | `../.ai.mlt` | `../.ai.mlt/skills/README.md` |

**Path resolution:** (1) use a filled path cell; empty → fall through. (2) Auto-discover: source dir S = `$AGENT_OS_SOURCE` (thin), `$REPO_ROOT/.ai` (fat), `$REPO_ROOT` (self-hosted); parent = `S/..`; sister = `<S basename with <fw> inserted before its last .segment>` (e.g. `pilo.ai.ui.logicbison` for source `pilo.ai.logicbison`; `.ai`-prefixed sources resolve `.ai.<fw>` directly), else legacy `.ai.<fw>`; missing = "not installed". (3) Before routing, verify the framework dir + its `skills/README.md` exist; if absent, route to `@ai-director` prefixed `[degraded: <framework> not installed]` — never route into the void. If your source dir name breaks discovery (e.g. `my-framework`), fill the path cells manually — deploy output lists what it checked.

### Read at conversation start / when relevant

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `START_HERE.md` | What to invoke now; forgetfulness checklist |
| `PROCESS_ROUTER.md` | Process Q&A; `@process-router` vs `@session-control status` |
| `DOCS_TECH_STACK.md` | Stack + verification commands |
| `.work/standards/REPLACE:CONVENTIONS_FILE` | Code layout, naming, maintainability |
| `.work/standards/REPLACE:FEATURE_STANDARD_FILE` | Feature SPEC lifecycle |
| `.work/standards/REPLACE:DIRECTORY_MAP_FILE` | Repo layout and boundaries |
| `.work/context/HANDOFF.md` | Session handoff |
| `docs/guides/workflows/README.md` | Workflow index and artifact matrix |

**Concept pack:** `concepts/README.md` (MOD-01–MOD-08). When a change touches architecture, coupling, latency, cost, ops load, AI-generated code, prompt architecture, or declarative infrastructure: list applicable concept ids, run matching `prompt.md` under `concepts/<name>/`, attach outputs to the PR or `### Concept / NFR registry` in `.work/plans/NEXT.md`; tag quantitative claims `measured` | `estimated` | `assumption` | `unknown`.

### Placeholder map

| Placeholder | Resolves to |
